This is a genuine security/DoS defect introduced by the diff: public endpoint, no rate lim

judged_text: EmbedController#best enqueues a RetrieveTopic job on every anonymous request carrying a novel embed_url, and the only throttle (a 60-second per-URL Redis key) lives inside the job, so varying the URL string bypasses it entirely and the endpoint has no rate limit. An attacker with a forged Referer floods the Sidekiq queue with fetch jobs — each of which can trigger a full RSS feed poll plus a page fetch — driving the Discourse server to request attacker-chosen URLs from the embeddable host at unbounded rate: background-job exhaustion DoS and use of the forum as a scraping amplifier against the embeddable host.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbedController#best`, which enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, with no controller-side throttling. The only throttle shown is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which runs during job execution and keys on the full `@embed_url` string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying the URL string bypasses it and still floods Sidekiq with queued jobs. `ensure_embeddable` only checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which can be forged by a client. Each executed job can also run `Jobs::PollFeed` (full feed fetch) and/or `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (HTTP fetch) via `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, enabling background-job exhaustion / outbound request amplification.
